degraded.note: FLOOR § 11's fx-degraded: one seat per non-live render a snapshot can carry — catching_up (oldest_unsent_age_s 4,000), stale (silent 11m), offline (silent 2h 06m), disabled — plus a live working seat badged fold_lag with derivation.fold_lag_ms 117,000 (1m 57s), and the live idle seat AT-D3-5's sleeper assertion compares the dark desks against in the same run. That idle seat's task is the tier-3 answer after a tier-1 title was dropped past its bound (task.source telemetry, task.degraded true), so its bubble carries T19's degraded note — the desk model's bubble.degraded_note, which Appendix B row 15's list-view guard must see at a non-default value on some run. The stale and offline seats carry delivery.no_data_since equal to delivery.last_receipt_at, and an idle activity_state underneath, which is what AT-D3-5's RED switches on. The run lasts 60 s so every dark age visibly advances and the lag number visibly does not; the feed.heartbeat at 30 s carries a newer server_time than the snapshot that delivered the derivation block, so a lag line stamped with the newest server_time the client saw, rather than the one that delivered the number, moves.

degraded_static.note: AT-D3-13 renders `fx-degraded` STATICALLY — its Build bullet says "render ... and capture a static image of each desk", and it asserts the log gains NO `edge` row. The `degraded` run beside this one is AT-D3-5's and delivers a `feed.heartbeat` at 30 s, which a conformant client answers with A14's and A17's rows (§ 6.2, § 11) — so replaying THAT run under AT-D3-13 would red a correct client, and "fixing" it by suppressing those two rows is the stopped-clock defect § 6.2 exists to prevent. § 6.4 states of AT-D3-13 that A17's driver "none of its fixtures deliver", and this run is what makes that true of the bytes.
